newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican ex-presidents in rare spat over murder case.
newsitem.headline: Mexican ex-presidents in rare spat over murder case.

text.p: In a break with tradition, two former Mexican presidents have engaged in a public spat linked to the murder of a presidential candidate, with one indirectly accusing the other of lying in comments published on Saturday.

The bickering is the latest development in the long-running saga of the 1994 murder of presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio, who as candidate of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) was poised to succeed then outgoing President Carlos Salinas de Gortari. In Mexico, outgoing presidents traditionally hand pick their successors.

In an interview with the influential Excelsior newspaper published on Saturday, Luis Echeverria, president from 1970 to 1976, denied he had tried to impose his preferred candidate on Salinas after Colosio was gunned down at a campaign rally in Tijuana. Echeverria was commenting on Salinas' assertion in a lengthy three-part interview published by the competing newspaper Reforma two weeks ago.

"Although to date the investigation has not turned up proof to confirm a conspiracy to kill Luis Donaldo, I do believe there was a conspiracy to try to impose a substitute," Salinas told Reforma, breaking a long silence from his self-imposed exile. "Those behind it seem to continue relentlessly in the tremendous struggle for power."

Salinas named Echeverria as one who tried to put forward his preferred substitute candidate, Emilio Gamboa Patron, the communications and transport minister at the time. But Echeverria told Excelsior: "I didn't propose anybody."
"How was I going to dare to involve myself in responsibilities?" he asked. "I'm retired (from politics), on the margin, with a clear conscience."
In the 67 years that the PRI has ruled in Mexico, outgoing presidents traditionally hand pick their successors and then fade into the background. They certainly do not criticise each other.

Salinas, in office from 1988 to 1994, had chosen Colosio to succeed him and eventually selected current President Ernesto Zedillo as candidate after Colosio was killed. The investigation into Colosio's murder has raised more questions than answers, with only one man, confessed gunman Mario Aburto, behind bars.
